summary: This section allows certain companies to have a special director chosen by small shareholders. A small shareholder is someone holding shares up to a certain small value. The rules for how this director is elected and their terms must follow official guidelines.
points: A listed company is permitted to have one director elected by small shareholders.
The election and terms of this director must follow prescribed rules.
Small shareholders are defined as those holding shares of a nominal value up to twenty thousand rupees or another prescribed sum.
example: Meera Textiles Private Limited is a listed company with many individual investors holding small amounts of shares. One of these investors, Ramesh, holds shares with a nominal value of fifteen thousand rupees. Because the company is allowed under the law to have a director chosen by small shareholders, Ramesh and other investors like him join together to elect a representative to the board. This director will voice the concerns of small investors during company meetings, following all the official rules and conditions set down for such appointments.

terms.meaning: A company that has its shares traded on a recognized stock exchange.
The face value of the shares as stated in the company documents.

watch: Do not assume every company must have this director, as the text says a listed company may have one.
